note: [agent-bulk] DRAG_CHECK FALSE NEGATIVE on this event (segments_redrew=false): scanbot_capture samples seg3_src.data.xs[0][0], which here is the first point of segment 16004 sitting 0.000003 cm from the main vertex - i.e. the rotation centre of the sweep, so it cannot move in screen-u and the absolute 1e-6 threshold can never be met. Frames are NOT stale: cloud_redrew true (-197.7 -> -319.4), d_az 0.7500 rad exactly as expected, all six vtx-*.png distinct md5 and 74-195 kB, and on vtx-az-055-el+20 vs vtx-az+065-el+20 the muon polyline swings from up-left to up-right and stays embedded in its own point cloud, which is the direct proof the segment source reprojects. Judged on that basis. VERDICT: shw 40019 (129.2 MeV, 3 seg, 39.9 cm) is not an EM shower. On both shw40019-az-055-el+20 and -az+085-el+20 it is a single straight uniformly-narrow line with a tight point cloud and no transverse development, no branching, no widening anywhere along ~38 cm (about 2.7 radiation lengths in LAr) - a minimum-ionising track. Its three members are collinear: the 1.5 cm seed 40019 at the X, a 0.7 cm stub 41020 at 16.4 cm / 3.7 deg, and 49023, a 37.70 cm pdg-13 segment at 21.3 cm / 4.2 deg absorbed by pass4_angle, which is 94 percent of the member length. ov-iso.png shows the whole event is ONE continuous ~155 cm line: the unowned 113.74 cm muon 16007 from the star, then this object beyond its far end (16007 reads 15.4 cm / 176.5 deg from 40019, i.e. directly behind the shower start). So the clustering of the three pieces into one object is defensible; what is wrong is calling the result a 129 MeV EM shower. Every other candidate is at 155-177 deg, behind the start, so there is no under-clustering claim and no over-clustering claim to make. Vertex: the star is at the end of the only track in the event; with a single prong there is nothing to converge, so I do not call it vertex-bad, but note there is no independent confirmation of it either. Scope: 2 showers of 17 examined; 15 skipped by the <20 MeV rule. The other in-scope shower 21009 (21.5 MeV, 1 seg, 2.6 cm) is 427 cm away from 40019 - a different region of the detector, pulled into scope only by the energy cut - and I did not scan it. The vtx-* sweep is half-span 232 cm here (driven by that 4 m separation) so it was used for topology only. Confidence likely not certain: no dQ/dx available, and I did not establish whether the 15 cm gap between 16007 and this object is a detector gap or a real break.
